title: The ISIZE at the end of gzip is the length modulo 2^32
summary: The CRC32 at the end of each member checks the decompressed bytes, and ISIZE records the lower 32 bits of its byte number. Both are little endian.
detail: ISIZE can be 0 when the member is decompressed to 2^32 bytes; this is the same as the length field of a truly empty member.
boundary: The tail value only describes the current member; the last four bytes cannot represent the complete decompression amount of the multi-member file.
relevance: Avoid treating the surrounding four-byte value as an exact total when determining attachment length.
